item.title: Java Concept Study Guide - 2025 Interview Questions
item.description:
Java Concept Study Guide - 2025 Interview Questions

Beginner (Basic Definitions & Keywords)

1. What is oops?

Answer: Object-Oriented Programming (OOPS) is a paradigm that uses “objects” to design software, focusing on data and its interactions.

2. What is inheritance?

Answer: A mechanism where one class (child) acquires the properties and behaviors of another class (parent).

3. Brief about encapsulation.

Answer: Bundling data and methods into a single unit (class) and hiding internal details using private.

item.title: Java Concept Study Guide - AiiTE Q Dump-Set_6
item.description:
Java Concept Study Guide - AiiTE Q Dump-Set_6

Beginner (Basic Syntax & OOPS Basics)

1. What is an abstract class? Provide an example.

Answer: A class that cannot be instantiated and is used as a base for other classes. Example: abstract class Animal { abstract void eat(); }.

2. What is Abstraction and where is it used?

Answer: Hiding implementation and showing only functionality. Used in Java through interfaces and abstract classes.

item.title: Java Concept Study Guide - AiiTE Q Dump-Set_7
item.description:
Java Concept Study Guide - AiiTE Q Dump-Set_7

Beginner (Fundamentals)

1. What is abstraction?

Answer: Abstraction is hiding the complex “how” and showing only the essential “what.” It simplifies interaction by focusing on functionality rather than implementation.

2. What is the static keyword?

Answer: It means the member belongs to the class, not to any specific object. It is shared across all instances.

3. What is the use of the super keyword?

Answer: To refer to the immediate parent class instance or to call the parent’s constructor.

item.title: Java Concept Study Guide - AiiTE Q Dump-Set_8_Update
item.description:
Java Concept Study Guide - AiiTE Q Dump-Set_8_Update

Beginner (Basics)

1. Explain the OOPS concepts.

Answer:

  • Encapsulation: Bundling data and code together.
  • Inheritance: Acquiring features from a parent class.
  • Polymorphism: One action performing in different ways.
  • Abstraction: Hiding internal details and showing functionality.

2. What is an abstract class in Java?

Answer: A class that cannot be instantiated and can contain both abstract methods (without body) and concrete methods (with body).

item.title: Java Concept Study Guide - Aiite Q Dump - Set_1
item.description:
Java Concept Study Guide - Aiite Q Dump - Set_1

Beginner (Basics & Definitions)

1. What are the data types in Java?

Answer: Primitives (e.g., int, char, boolean) and Non-Primitives (e.g., String, Array, Classes).

2. Explain the super and this keywords.

Answer: this refers to the current class instance; super refers to the immediate parent class instance.

3. What is the new keyword in Java?

Answer: Used to create a new object and allocate memory on the heap.

item.title: Java Concept Study Guide - Aiite Q Dump - Set_2
item.description:
Java Concept Study Guide - Aiite Q Dump - Set_2

Beginner (Basics)

1. What is the difference between a class and an object?

Answer: A class is a blueprint or template; an object is a physical instance of that blueprint.

2. What are Primitives and Non-Primitive data types?

Answer: Primitives (e.g., int, boolean) store simple values; Non-Primitives (e.g., String, Array) are complex objects and store references.

3. Is String a primitive or non-primitive data type?

Answer: Non-primitive. It is a class in Java.

item.title: Java Concept Study Guide - Aiite Q Dump - Set_3
item.description:
Java Concept Study Guide - Aiite Q Dump - Set_3

Beginner (Basics)

1. What is a Variable?

Answer: A container that holds data during the execution of a program (e.g., int x = 10;).

2. Difference between Local and Global variables.

Answer:

  • Local: Declared inside a method; visible only within that method.
  • Global (Instance): Declared inside a class but outside methods; visible to all methods in the class.

3. Explain Looping statements.

Answer: Statements that execute a block of code repeatedly as long as a condition is true (e.g., for, while, do-while).

item.title: Java Concept Study Guide - Aiite Q Dump - Set_4
item.description:
Java Concept Study Guide - Aiite Q Dump - Set_4

Beginner (Basics)

1. Explain the OOPS concepts.

Answer:

  • Inheritance: Reuse code from parent.
  • Polymorphism: One name, many forms.
  • Encapsulation: Secure data in a unit.
  • Abstraction: Show essential features.

2. What are the access specifiers in Java?

Answer: public (anywhere), private (class only), protected (package + child), default (package only).

3. Difference between JDK and JRE.

Answer: JRE (Runtime) runs the programs; JDK (Development Kit) contains tools like compiler (javac) to create programs.

item.title: Java Concept Study Guide - Aiite Q Dump -Set_5
item.description:
Java Concept Study Guide - Aiite Q Dump -Set_5

Beginner (Basics)

1. Provide examples of Abstraction, Interface, and Encapsulation.

Answer:

  • Abstraction: A BasePage defining click() without defining the logic.
  • Interface: WebDriver defining browser actions.
  • Encapsulation: Private locators accessed via public login() method.

2. Explain Inheritance and its types.

Answer: Sharing code between parent and child classes. Types: Single, Multilevel, Hierarchical.

3. What are the Access Modifiers and their scopes?

Answer: public (anywhere), private (same class), protected (package+child), default (same package).

item.description:
Java-related Concept Study Guide - Cucmber_QuestionDump_Set_1,2,3,4

Beginner (Basics)

1. What is the use of pom.xml in your project?

Answer: It is the Project Object Model file for Maven. It manages the project’s dependencies, plugins, and build configurations.

2. What are the dependencies used in your project?

Answer: Common dependencies include selenium-java, cucumber-java, junit or testng, and apache-poi for Excel reading.

Intermediate (Configuration & Usage)

3. Other than dependencies, what else is present in the pom.xml file?

Answer: It contains plugins (like maven-surefire-plugin), properties (like Java version), and project metadata (name, version, groupID).

item.title: Java Concept Study Guide - Java Q_Set_1_and_2
item.description:
Java Concept Study Guide - Java Q_Set_1_and_2

Beginner (Fundamentals)

1. What is the use of the main method in Java?

Answer: It is the entry point of any Java program. JVM starts execution from public static void main(String[] args).

2. Difference between a class and an object?

Answer: A Class is a blueprint/design; an Object is a physical instance of that class.

3. What is the Scanner class?

Answer: A built-in class used to capture user input from the console.

item.title: Java Ecosystem (Maven) Concept Study Guide - Maven_QuestionDump_Set_,1,2,3,4
item.description:
Java Ecosystem (Maven) Concept Study Guide - Maven_QuestionDump_Set_,1,2,3,4

Beginner

1. Explain Maven and its purpose.

Answer: Maven is a build automation and project management tool. Its primary purpose is to manage project dependencies, automate the build process (compiling, testing, packaging), and provide a uniform project structure.

2. Why are you using Maven in your project?

Answer: To simplify dependency management (no need to manually download JARs), automate builds, and ensure consistent environments across the team.

item.title: Java Ecosystem (TestNG) Concept Study Guide - TestNG_QuestionDump_Set_1_2_3
item.description:
Java Ecosystem (TestNG) Concept Study Guide - TestNG_QuestionDump_Set_1_2_3

Beginner

1. What is TestNG and explain why and where it is required?

Answer: TestNG is a testing framework inspired by JUnit but introducing new functionalities like grouping, parameterization, and dependency testing. It is required for sophisticated automation suites where test control is essential.

2. What are the advantages of TestNG?

Answer: Support for annotations, data-driven testing (via @DataProvider), parallel execution, prioritizing tests, and generating detailed HTML reports.

Java Concept Answers - oops.md

Beginner (Fundamentals)

What is OOPS?

Object-Oriented Programming (OOPS) is a way of designing software using “objects” that represent real-world things. These objects have data (attributes) and actions (methods).

What is the difference between a Class and an Object?

  • Class: A blueprint or template (e.g., a “Car” design).
  • Object: A real instance of that blueprint (e.g., your specific “Red Tesla”).

Explain the “four pillars” of OOPS:

  1. Encapsulation: Hiding data to keep it safe (using private).
  2. Inheritance: Sharing features from a parent to a child (using extends).
  3. Polymorphism: One thing having many forms (e.g., Overloading and Overriding).
  4. Abstraction: Showing only essential features and hiding the complex logic.

What is the syntax for declaring, initializing, and accessing arrays in Java?

  • Declare: int[] arr;
  • Initialize: arr = new int[5];
  • Access: arr[0] = 10;

What is the difference between an Abstract Class and an Interface?

  • Abstract Class: Can have both finished methods and unfinished (abstract) methods. Used for “is-a” relationships.
  • Interface: A contract that says “what to do,” not “how to do it.” Used for “can-do” behaviors.

Intermediate (Practical Concepts & Implementation)

Explain the key principles of OOPS:

  • Modularity: Breaking code into small, manageable pieces.
  • Reusability: Using existing code in new programs.
  • Security: Protecting data through encapsulation.

How is OOPS implemented in Java specifically?

Java uses classes to define objects, private fields for encapsulation, extends for inheritance, and interfaces for abstraction.

Java Ecosystem (TestNG) Concept Answers - TestNG_QuestionDump_Set_1_2_3.md

What is TestNG?

TestNG is a Testing Framework for Java. It is more advanced than JUnit and provides features like grouping, prioritizing, and parameterization.

List TestNG annotations execution order:

  1. @BeforeSuite
  2. @BeforeTest
  3. @BeforeClass
  4. @BeforeMethod
  5. @Test
  6. @AfterMethod
  7. @AfterClass
  8. @AfterTest
  9. @AfterSuite

What is a Data Provider?

A TestNG feature that allows you to run a single test method multiple times with different sets of data.

How to rerun failed test cases?

  • Manual: Run the testng-failed.xml file generated in the test-output folder.
  • Automatic: Implement the IRetryAnalyzer interface.

How to set priority?

Use the priority attribute in the @Test annotation. @Test(priority = 1) (Note: If no priority is set, tests run alphabetically. Negative priorities run first.)
